title: Residue transcendence degree decreases under scheme base change and has an equality lift
statement: Let $f:U\to B$ be a locally finite type morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $g:B'\to B$ be any scheme morphism. Form $U'=U\times_BB'$ with projections $q:U'\to U$ and $f':U'\to B'$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Residue fields and their induced maps are [def-weil-residue-field], and transcendence degrees are [def-kun-transcendence-degree]. For every $u'\in U'$, put $u=q(u')$, $b'=f'(u')$ and $b=f(u)$. Then $$\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(b')}\kappa(u')\leq\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(b)}\kappa(u).$$ Conversely, for every $u\in U$ and $b'\in B'$ satisfying $g(b')=f(u)$, there exists $u'\in U'$ with $q(u')=u$, $f'(u')=b'$, and $$\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(b')}\kappa(u')=\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(u))}\kappa(u).$$ No flatness, surjectivity, separation, quasi-compactness or Noetherian hypothesis on $g$, $U$ or $B$ is imposed. Empty schemes are allowed.

proof.text: Fix compatible $u,b'$ and put $b=f(u)=g(b')$, $k=\kappa(b)$ and $K=\kappa(b')$. The residue-field map makes $K/k$ a field extension [def-weil-residue-field]. Choose an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ about $b$ and a finite-type affine chart $W=\operatorname{Spec}S$ about $u$ in $f^{-1}(V)$, using the definition of locally finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Choose an affine open $V'=\operatorname{Spec}R'$ about $b'$ in $g^{-1}(V)$. Fibre-product pasting and the affine-spectrum tensor-product theorem identify the open chart $W\times_VV'$ of $U'$ with $\operatorname{Spec}C$, $C=S\otimes_RR'$, compatibly with both projections [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting, lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. For a prescribed $u'$ this chart contains $u'$; for the existence assertion it suffices to produce a point in this chart. Explicitly, the open subset $q^{-1}(W)\cap(f')^{-1}(V')$ has the same universal property as $W\times_VV'$: maps into it are exactly pairs of maps into $W,V'$ agreeing in $V$, since factorization through an open subscheme is unique. Thus the chart identification follows from [def-pc-fibre-product]. Restriction to an open neighbourhood preserves residue fields because neighbourhoods inside that open are cofinal in the stalk colimit.

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak r\subset R$ and $\mathfrak r'\subset R'$ represent $b,b'$. Set $A=S\otimes_Rk$ and $T=A\otimes_kK$. The defining bilinear relations give $T\simeq S\otimes_RK\simeq C\otimes_{R'}K$: $(s\otimes a)\otimes\lambda\mapsto s\otimes a\lambda$ and $(s\otimes r')\otimes\lambda\mapsto s\otimes\overline{r'}\lambda$, with inverses inserting units. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-primes-residue-fields] to $R\to S$ over $\mathfrak r$, and to $R'\to C$ over $\mathfrak r'$. It identifies $u$ with a prime $\mathfrak p$ of $A$ and the points of $\operatorname{Spec}C$ over $b'$ with primes $P$ of $T$, with their residue fields identified over $k$ and $K$, respectively. Contraction $P\cap A=\mathfrak p$ is exactly the requirement that the corresponding point projects to $u$: the explicit inverse kernels $s\otimes a\mapsto\overline s\,\overline a$ in the cited theorem commute with the two displayed tensor maps. Thus it remains to compare $\operatorname{trdeg}_K\kappa(P)$ with $\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and to choose $P$ above $\mathfrak p$ attaining equality.

proof.text: A finite set of $R$-algebra generators of $S$ gives $k$-algebra generators of $A$; tensoring once more gives $K$-algebra generators of $T$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Hence both $A$ and $T$ are Noetherian by [lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components]. The map $j:A\to T$, $a\mapsto a\otimes1$, is faithfully flat by [lem-weil-pbc-field-extension-base-change-faithfully-flat], and therefore flat by [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map]. These assertions require no Noetherian hypothesis on $R,R'$ or on either original base scheme.

source.place: Tag 02FY (lemma-dimension-fibre-after-base-change), parts (2),(3); reduction to Algebra Tag 0CWE (lemma-inequalities-under-field-extension)

proof.text: For every prime $P$ of $T$ contracting to $\mathfrak p$, put $h=\dim A_{\mathfrak p}$, $h'=\dim T_P$, $r=\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and $r'=\operatorname{trdeg}_K\kappa(P)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-field-extension] to the finite-type $k$-algebra $A$ and $K/k$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-local-ring-trdeg] to $(k,A,\mathfrak p)$ and $(K,T,P)$. They give the finite-integer equality $h+r=h'+r'$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-height-formula] to the flat map $A\to T$ of Noetherian rings: it gives $h'=h+e$, where $e=\operatorname{ht}(P/\mathfrak pT)\geq0$. Here $\mathfrak pT\subset P$ by contraction. The height is the supremum of prime-chain lengths below $P/\mathfrak pT$, so its nonnegativity follows from the length-zero chain at that prime, as in the cited height formula. Finiteness of $h'$ also makes $e$ finite.

source.place: Tag 02FY (lemma-dimension-fibre-after-base-change), parts (2),(3); reduction to Algebra Tag 0CWE (lemma-inequalities-under-field-extension)

proof.text: Substitution and cancellation in the finite integers give $r=e+r'$, hence $r'\leq r$. For a prescribed $u'$, its prime $P$ in step 2 contracts to $\mathfrak p$, so the residue-field identifications there give exactly the required inequality. No claim that all lifts have equality is made: the nonnegative term $e$ measures their possible loss of transcendence degree.

source.place: Tag 02FY (lemma-dimension-fibre-after-base-change), parts (2),(3); reduction to Algebra Tag 0CWE (lemma-inequalities-under-field-extension)

proof.text: To attain equality, use [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-surjective-spectrum] for $j$ to choose a prime $P_0$ of $T$ above $\mathfrak p$. The ideal $\mathfrak pT$ lies in $P_0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-prime-contains-minimal-prime], there is a prime $P\subseteq P_0$ minimal over $\mathfrak pT$. Its contraction contains $\mathfrak p$ because $\mathfrak pT\subseteq P$, and is contained in $\mathfrak p$ because $P\subseteq P_0$. Thus it contracts exactly to $\mathfrak p$. There is no strictly smaller prime of $T/\mathfrak pT$ contained in $P/\mathfrak pT$, by this minimality; consequently its height is zero by the prime-chain definition in [lem-weil-pbc-flat-height-formula]. Applying the calculation of step 4 to this $P$ gives $h'=h$ and then $r'=r$.

source.place: Tag 02FY (lemma-dimension-fibre-after-base-change), parts (2),(3); reduction to Algebra Tag 0CWE (lemma-inequalities-under-field-extension)

proof.text: By the bijection and residue-field isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-primes-residue-fields] used in step 2, this $P$ gives a point $u'$ of $\operatorname{Spec}C\subset U'$ mapping to $b'$, and contraction to $\mathfrak p$ gives $q(u')=u$. Its $K$-residue field is $\kappa(P)$, so $r'=r$ is precisely the stated equality. If no compatible pair $u,b'$ exists, the existence assertion has no instance. If $U'$ is empty the inequality is vacuous; a compatible pair would produce the point just constructed. Thus empty schemes and arbitrary $g$ cause no exception.
